title: I finally started learning game development!
author: Hilipilihei
selftext:
Hey everyone!

A short backstory: I'm a 44 years old male, got ADHD and Asperger diagnoses as an adult. I wanted to make a game since I was a small kid with a Commodore 64 and NES but my attention span never let me learn anything further. I did try some coding (BASIC), animation (Deluxe Paint III), image editing (Photoshop), music (Ultimate Soundtracker) but nothing ever lead anywhere and by mid to late 90s everything was already so professional that the dream of me ever making a game by myself had died.

A few years ago that dream re-emerged because I played many indie games made by solo devs or very small teams (Axiom Verge, Cyber Shadow, HROT, Dusk, Cultic, Terraria, Stardew Valley, Cave Story, Braid, etc.) and 3,5 months ago I finally decided to start learning. Also modern generative AI tools are at that point where you can speed up the learning and development processes considerably.

I'm using Godot and I just released my fifth prototype game (overall) but basically the first one that I actually wanted to make. It's the first one to use scrolling, parallax scrolling, multiple playable characters, real pixel art (damn that 320x180 resolution was restrictive! never again!), score calculating ceremony, etc.

My main focus is game design but small sprites, animation, sound effects (based on free stock library sound effects) and writing were done by me. Of course I had to be heavily involved with all graphics and code as well. I used Suno for most music and ChatGPT for code and image generation.

It's a 2D skateboarding side-scroller with punk, hip hop and graffiti influences. It started as a small inside joke for my skate posse but eventually grew a bit bigger. It's very simple but pretty fun in my opinion. I spent around 8 weeks and 400-500 hours to make this. I'd appreciate to get some feedback from other developers, mainly on game design, fun factor :) Thanks!

  
[https://ruderalis.itch.io/skate-and-die](https://ruderalis.itch.io/skate-and-die)

I hope that with time I could rely less on AI assist, do more assets by myself, and do some collaboration with other people but so far I have very little to show of my supposed game designer talents :)

comments.author: loontoon
comments.body:
Well done getting started!  

I love the intro - some very clever jokes like the ADHD thing and the FBI warning LOL!  Definitely my sense of humour!

comments.author: bombero_kmn
comments.body:
Wow, this is actually eerie, I'm the same age and same backstory almost exactly, and sitting here working on my own game in Claude based on a 90s feel, and also in Godot, and I haven't touched a line of code or made an asset myself. 

Which is really encouraging for me, to see others doing the same so ty for sharing! 

Live thoughts:

JFC this is great. From the "winners don't lose drugs" to the splash screen - I haven't even started yet and I love it. 

Nice transition from splash to menu, I like the musical variety. Nice detail in the bg, I'm already primed to look for visual easter eggs. 

Still not playing yet bc this track slaps. Menu is well organized though! 

Skater select: detail level in the profiles is nice, but what's the difference between them? Does red, green, yellow relate to difficulty ? Do they have different stats? 

Details on both the background and the cars is impressive, play is pretty smooth. I've died several times and had fun doing so. 

The end screen is just icing on the cake. 

Overall really impressive, ty again for sharing. Definitely sets a high bar for my own game lol. Keep it up!

replies.author: Hilipilihei
replies.body:
Nice to hear I'm not the only one who started to learn game development very late in life and had to start from the basics :)

You must also know that making an AI assisted game is not like just writing a prompt "Mr. AI, make me this 2D side-scrolling retro pixel-art skateboarding game with beer, pooping, punk, instrumental hip hop, graffiti, cops, etc." and then magically 5 mins later it's done but you have to learn how to use Godot (or Unity, or UE, or...), what are scenes, scripts, inspector, different nodes... what kind of structure, autoload managers, etc. you should have.   
  
I haven't tried anything else than ChatGPT but a lot of people have been recommending Claude so probably I'm gonna try that next, but at least with ChatGPT you have to learn how to properly command it.. otherwise you'll end up in a situation where ownerships are spread everywhere, you have multiple god scripts and trying to add something means rewriting, deleting and changing things. Eventually you'll understand more and more of it and can do edits in scripts by yourself.

Thanks also for the feedback, I appreciate it! Most of the feedback has been either "It's super rad! I love it!" or "WTF is this AI slop?" so it's nice to hear a bit more detailed which parts you liked, etc. I had plans to have different stats, perhaps different tricks and so on for the different skaters but I came to conclusion that it would be difficult to balance it and it would've taken unnecessary long and I just wanted to get it done as it had already been well over my estimated 2-3 weeks.

But I just had to have 3 skaters as this thing started as an inside joke / gift to my skate posse called PaSkA (means Shit in Finnish but at the same time it's short for Parta-, Skeittaus- ja Alkoholikerho which means Beard, Skateboarding and Alcohol Club) so the only difference between them is graphics and song that's playing during the game. There's also many references to my hometown Helsinki and some jokes are in Finnish but you won't actually miss much as most of it is in English :)

Good luck with your project!
